Why Motorcycle Camping Is Magic

Motorcycle camping combines two of life's great pleasures — riding and sleeping under the stars. It frees you from hotel booking constraints, saves significant money on accommodation, and puts you closer to the landscapes you have come to explore. Some of the best camping spots in the UK — wild Highlands, coastal cliffs, forest clearings — are accessible only to those willing to pack light and live simply.

The Essential Camping Kit

Space and weight are critical constraints when camping by motorcycle. Every item must earn its place in your panniers:

  • Tent — A lightweight 1-2 person tent weighing under 2kg. Look for quick-pitch designs and waterproof ratings of at least 3,000mm HH for British conditions.
  • Sleeping bag — A 3-season bag rated to around 0 degrees Celsius handles most UK camping from April to October. Down is lighter but synthetic performs better when damp.
  • Sleeping mat — An inflatable or self-inflating mat provides insulation and comfort. Look for compact packed size and an R-value of at least 3 for UK spring and autumn camping.
  • Cooking system — A compact stove, small gas canister, and lightweight pot for hot drinks and simple meals.
  • Head torch — Essential for setting up camp in the dark and navigating to facilities at night.

Packing Strategy

Divide your camping gear between panniers for even weight distribution. The tent goes on top of one pannier for quick access. The sleeping bag can be compressed and stuffed in the bottom of the other pannier. Cooking gear lives in the tank bag or tail pack for easy access at camp.

Best Camping Spots for Motorcycle Tourers

Wild camping is legal in Scotland under the Outdoor Access Code. In England and Wales, stick to designated campsites unless you have landowner permission. The best motorcycle-friendly campsites have flat pitches for bikes, covered areas for drying gear, and are within riding distance of good roads.

Popular motorcycle camping sites include Applecross Campsite on the NC500, Hooks House Farm in the Yorkshire Dales, Eweleaze Farm in Dorset, and Trwyn yr Wylfa on Anglesey. Book ahead during peak season as motorcycle-friendly pitches fill quickly.

Keep your camping gear in waterproof dry bags inside your panniers. Even with waterproof luggage, condensation and splash can dampen gear over a multi-day tour. A wet sleeping bag at the end of a long riding day is deeply miserable.

Wild Camping Considerations

In Scotland, wild camping is legal under the Outdoor Access Code, allowing you to pitch your tent in most open areas. Always leave no trace and move on within a day or two. In England and Wales, wild camping generally requires landowner permission.

faq.q: What is the essential motorcycle camping kit?
faq.a: The core kit is a lightweight tent under 2kg, a 3-season sleeping bag rated to around 0C, an insulated sleeping mat with an R-value of at least 3, a compact cooking system and a head torch. Space and weight are the key constraints, so every item must earn its place in your panniers. Buy compact, packable versions of everything.

faq.q: How do I pack camping gear on a motorcycle?
faq.a: Divide the gear between panniers for even weight distribution. Put the tent on top of one pannier for quick access on arrival, and compress the sleeping bag into the bottom of the other. Cooking gear lives in a tank bag or tail pack where you can reach it easily at camp. Keep the heaviest items low to protect handling.

faq.q: Should I choose a down or synthetic sleeping bag?
faq.a: Down is lighter and packs smaller, but it loses insulation when damp and is slow to dry, which is a real risk in the British climate. Synthetic bags are bulkier but keep insulating even when wet and dry faster. For UK motorcycle camping, many riders prefer synthetic for its reliability, or a down bag kept scrupulously dry in a waterproof stuff sack.

faq.q: Is wild camping legal in the UK?
faq.a: In Scotland, wild camping is legal under the Outdoor Access Code, allowing you to pitch in most open areas provided you leave no trace and move on within a day or two. In England and Wales, wild camping generally requires the landowner's permission, so stick to designated campsites unless you have arranged otherwise.

faq.q: How do I keep my gear dry on a multi-day tour?
faq.a: Pack everything in waterproof dry bags inside your panniers. Even with waterproof luggage, condensation and road splash can dampen gear over several days. Keep your sleeping bag in a sealed dry bag at all costs, because a wet sleeping bag at the end of a long, cold riding day is one of the most miserable camping experiences there is.
